thread:
hana: quick flag  onboarding qlite2-int8: we see rare malformed funcall JSONs when streaming + funcalls are enabled. ~0.15% but reproducible under load. anyone seen streaming split produce NULs or replacement chars?

gopal: can you drop a raw snippet + runtime flags? model variant, serializer, kv_prefix?

hana: runtime=staging, model=qlite2-int8, streaming=true, funcalls=true, serializer=ndjson, kv_prefix=true. snippet: 

hana: ```
{"tool":"search","args":{"q":"cheap flights"}}

\x00\xef\xbf\xbd

{"tool":"book","args":{"id":42}}
```

ira: that looks like NUL then replacement char. suggests either zero padding or truncated multibyte sequence. is this correlated with longer sequences / bigger batches?

hana: yes—spikes when seq_len>700 and batch>=12. single-model non-streaming runs are clean.

build-bot: Canary snapshot (qlite2-int8, last 8h): total=61,234, parse_failures=92 (0.15%), streaming=true in 88% of failures, seq_len>700 in 81% of failures.

gopal: immediate mitigation: (A) add 1 fast repair retry (non-streaming) for structured toolcalls; (B) sanitizer that strips only \x00 and isolates U+FFFD then retry. low-risk while we root cause.

hana: agreed. i'll enable sanitizer+retry in canary path and pin seq_len>700 to qlite2-fp16 fallback.

ira: triage plan: 1) reproduce locally forcing chunk splits inside multibyte utf8 (seq=820, batch=14); 2) capture per-chunk raw hex + token ids for failures; 3) run with kv_prefix off to check correlation; 4) try zero-fill microbatch tails before dequant in runtime staging.

gopal: also instrument chunk checksums on the streamer boundary to detect in-flight corruption or re-chunking from proxy. if checksums mismatch we know it's network/proxy.

hana: quick local replay with null-strip sanitizer reduced failures from 28 -> 3 over 30m. remaining 3 show U+FFFD in decoder output which sanitizer doesn't fix.

ira: that residual points to truncated multibyte sequences or kernel emitting garbage. i'll grep recent kernel commits for int8 streaming patches. if there's a buffer reuse optimization, it could explain uninitialized bytes.

gopal: low-effort runtime experiment: zero-pad last microbatch bytes before dequant. if residual failures disappear we likely had uninitialized tail bytes. can we roll that in staging?

hana: i'll run zero-pad test in staging and post results in ~2h. also uploading captured artifacts (token id diffs + chunk checksums) to the canary bucket for the kernel team.

build-bot: routing change applied: seq_len>700 -> qlite2-fp16 fallback for 3h. Monitoring parse_failures.

gopal: if zero-pad works, schedule a small runtime patch and a canary deploy. if not, next step is to disable buffer reuse in ndjson streamer and re-run.

hana: thanks all. leaving thread open; will update when zero-pad experiment finishes. :hourglass:
